title: CORE  of the EU DPP core ontology proposed by the CIRPASS-2 project.
description:
The CORE is the integration ontology that imports all the specific ontology modules and the connector (bridge) ontology of these.

--
THIS DOCUMENT IS PROVIDED WITH NO WARRANTIES WHATSOEVER. 
All liability for any damages arising from use or misuse of this vocabulary is with the user.

classes.label: Actor
classes.comment: Actor means a legal or natural person (e.g. John Doe, TNO). One actor can take on multiple roles; [CIRPASS-2 User Stories 3.1]

classes.label: Actor role assignment
classes.comment: Assigns a role to the actor in a particular context (DPP, Product, Event).

classes.label: Aggregation Event
classes.comment: A technical event carrier representing the aggregation or disaggregation of child objects under a parent object, typically reflecting packaging, containment, or structural hierarchy changes. Each AggregationEvent has exactly one action type, may refer to at most one parent object identifier, and includes at least one child object identifier, at least one child quantity context, or both.
classes.source: GS1 EPCIS 2.0; adapted from the Event module mapping table.

classes.label: Air Pollution Footprint
classes.comment: Quantifies the release of airborne pollutants (e.g., particulate matter, photochemical ozone formation) over the life cycle of a product. AirPollutionFootprint is an ImpactResult associated with relevant environmental impact categories.

classes.label: Association Event
classes.comment: A technical event carrier introduced in the EU DPP Core Ontology to represent the association, dissociation, or observation of relationships between identifiable objects without implying physical aggregation or parent-child containment semantics. Each AssociationEvent has exactly one action type, may refer to at most one association anchor, and includes at least one associated child object identifier, at least one child quantity context, or both.
classes.source: Defined in the EU DPP Core Ontology Event module as an EPCIS-inspired extension for expressing non-containment associations between identified entities.

classes.label: Authorised representative role assignment
classes.comment: A specific assignment representing the written mandate between a manufacturer and an authorised representative; [ESPR Art 2 (43)]

classes.label: Business Location
classes.comment: A location playing the role of business context, indicating where the event is considered to take place from a business perspective.
classes.source: GS1 EPCIS 2.0; business location concept adapted for the Event module.

classes.label: Business Transaction Context
classes.comment: A contextual structure representing a business transaction associated with a transaction event.
classes.source: Adapted from GS1 EPCIS business transaction list semantics for the EU DPP Core Ontology Event module.

classes.label: Business Transaction Type
classes.comment: A classification indicating the business type of a transaction associated with an event.
classes.source: Adapted from GS1 CBV business transaction type semantics for the EU DPP Core Ontology Event module.

classes.label: Circular Economy Indicator
classes.comment:
Circular Economy indicators are measures for relevant monitoring the transition to a circular economy and to measure the effects of new policy and trends.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: ClassificationCode
classes.comment: A classification code from some product classification scheme .

classes.label: Common Specification
classes.comment: Common specification means ecodesign requirements, essential requirements for digital product passports or test, measurement or calculation methods established by implementing acts adopted by the Commission for products covered by delegated acts pursuant to ESPR Article 4.

classes.label: Concentration of the substance of concern
classes.comment: The concentration of the substances of concern, at the level of the product, its relevant components, or spare parts ESPR Art 7(5)

classes.label: Concentration of the substance of concern
classes.comment: The concentration of the substances of concern, at the level of the product, its relevant components, or spare parts ESPR Art 7(5)

classes.label: Conformity Certificate
classes.comment: Conformity assessment certificate for a certification. The blue guide uses the term "cerficate of conformity". The ESPR uses "conformity certificate" as well as "certificate" and "approval decision".
classes.source: Commission notice The ‘Blue Guide’ on the implementation of EU product rules 2022 Annex 4, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=oj:JOC_2022_247_R_0001

classes.label: Destruction
classes.comment: The intentional damaging or discarding of a product and unsold products as waste, with the exception of discarding for the sole purpose of delivering the discarded product for preparing for reuse, including refurbishment or remanufacturing operations. ESPR Art 2(34) and Art 25(1).

classes.label: DigitalInstruction
classes.comment:
Digital instructions
mean instructions in digital format concerning the product (‘digital instructions’) in a language that can be easily understood. ESPR Art 27(7)
Digital instructions are ensured by manufacturers. These should also ensured by importers. (ESPR Art 29(4))

This class can be extended/specialised according to delegated acts or industry standards.

classes.label: Document
classes.comment: The document class describes the semantic representation of any instance of a document that might be required to be included into a digital product passport instance.

classes.label: Digital Product Passport (DPP)
classes.comment:
Digital Product Passport (DPP) means a set of data specific to a product that includes the information specified in the applicable
delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4 and that is accessible via electronic means through a data carrier in accordance with Chapter III. (ESPR Art 2 (28))

classes.label: DPP Archival Event
classes.comment: An event corresponding to the archival or end-of-active-life management of a Digital Product Passport.

classes.label: DPP Creation Event
classes.comment: An event corresponding to the creation or initial issuance of a Digital Product Passport.

classes.label: DPP Event
classes.comment: An ESPR-level event concept representing an event that affects the existence, content, accessibility, update, correction, or governance of a DPP. A DPPEvent captures the passport-facing semantics of the occurrence and is modelled as distinct from the product event that may trigger it.

classes.label: DPP Event Record
classes.comment: A technical audit record used to represent and log an information-level event affecting a Digital Product Passport. Unlike EPCIS carriers, this class is intended for recording DPP-side information events rather than product-facing operational events.
classes.source: Defined in the EU DPP Core Ontology Event module to support the technical recording of DPP-related events.

classes.label: DPP Update Event
classes.comment: An event corresponding to an update of the content of a Digital Product Passport.

classes.label: Durability
classes.comment:
Durability
means the ability of a product to maintain over time its function and performance under specified conditions of use, maintenance and repair. (ESPR Art 2 (22))

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Emission to air
classes.comment:
Product parameters are listed in the ESPR Annex I :

(q) emissions to air, water or soil released in one or more lifecycle stages of the product as expressed through quantities and nature of emissions, including noise.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Emission to soil
classes.comment:
Product parameters are listed in the ESPR Annex I :

(q) emissions to air, water or soil released in one or more lifecycle stages of the product as expressed through quantities and nature of emissions, including noise.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Emission to water
classes.comment:
Product parameters are listed in the ESPR Annex I :

(q) emissions to air, water or soil released in one or more lifecycle stages of the product as expressed through quantities and nature of emissions, including noise.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Energy consumption
classes.comment:
Energy consumption of the product.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Energy Footprint
classes.comment: Quantifies the total energy use associated with a product throughout its life cycle, including renewable and non-renewable sources. EnergyFootprint is a FlowResult linked to the Energy FlowType.

classes.label: Environmental emission
classes.comment:
Emission is the act or amount of sending out gas, heat, light, etc. It can also refer to harmful substances that are released into the environment, especially carbon dioxide.


This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Environmental footprint
classes.comment:
Environmental footprint
means a quantification of the environmental impacts resulting from a product throughout its life
cycle, whether in relation to a single environmental impact category or an aggregated set of impact
categories based on the Product Environmental Footprint method established by Recommendation
(EU) 2 021/2279 or other scientific methods developed by international organisations, widely tested
in collaboration with different industry sectors and adopted or implemented by the Commission in
other Union law. (ESPR Art 2 (24)).

Product parameters list ESPR Annex I
(m) The environmental footprint of the product, expressed as a quantification;

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Environmental pollution
classes.comment:
Environmental pollution is the addition of any substance or form of energy to the environment at a rate faster than it can be dispersed or safely stored.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: EPCIS Carrier
classes.comment: A technical event class used as the abstract root of the Event carrier module. It represents a journalisation structure carrying the core event dimensions and serving as the superclass of specialised EPCIS-aligned event types. It is not itself a regulatory lifecycle event.
classes.source: Derived from GS1 EPCIS 2.0 and adapted for the EU DPP Core Ontology Event module.

classes.label: ESPR Event
classes.comment: Abstract superclass introduced for modelling purposes. Used to represent the regulatory or business semantics of an event relevant in the ESPR context and concerning either a product or its DPP, independently of its technical journalisation.
classes.source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781; lifecycle-event-oriented abstraction introduced for modelling purposes.

classes.label: EU Declaration of Conformity
classes.comment: The EU Declaration of Conformity shall state that the fulfilment of the ecodesign requirements specified in the applicable delegated acts adopted pursuant to ESPR Article 4 has been demonstrated or that a presumption of conformity applies in accordance with ESPR Article 41.
classes.source: Decision No 768/2008/EC Annex I Art R10, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dec/2008/768(1)/oj#anx_I

classes.label: Eutrophication Footprint
classes.comment: Quantifies nutrient enrichment impacts (eutrophication) on freshwater, marine, or terrestrial ecosystems caused by a product during its life cycle. It aggregates relevant ImpactCategories.

classes.label: Facility
classes.comment: A Facility may be a place where specific activities occur. A production/manufacturing facility means a factory. The term may refer to any place that makes things, or plants that generate electricity.

classes.label: Facility identifier
classes.comment: A unique code assigned to a physical site (factory, warehouse, plant, school, hospital, etc.), i.e., identifies a location.

classes.label: Flow Type
classes.comment: A category representing the type of flow quantified in a life cycle assessment. It is used to classify FlowResults according to the kind of resource or emission being measured.

classes.label: Harmonised Standard
classes.comment: Harmonised Standard means a European standard adopted on the basis of a request made by the Commission for the application of Union harmonisation legislation.

classes.label: Hazardous waste amount
classes.comment:
Hazardous waste amount of the product.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Height
classes.comment: Height of the product

classes.label: Identifier
classes.comment:
Identifier. A general class to hold different kinds of identifiers described and used for EU DPP CO. Each sub-class of this class describes a different kind of identifier. Intentionally modelled as sub-classes. 
Identifiers have value, and a scheme/standard they are based on.

Cardinatlity restrictions added to each subclass to enforce inheritance of the data propertyy identifierValue.

classes.label: Identifier granularity
classes.comment: The granularity of the identifier. For example, for Productys this could be model, batch, item.

classes.label: Identifier scheme
classes.comment: The scheme or standard

classes.label: Instance Identifier
classes.comment: An identifier-based structure used to represent an object identified at instance level in an EPCIS-inspired event context.
classes.source: Defined for the EU DPP Core Ontology Event module following EPCIS instance-level identification semantics.

classes.label: Land Footprint
classes.comment: Quantifies the occupation and transformation of land caused by a product throughout its life cycle. LandFootprint is an ImpactResult linked to the LandUse impact category.

classes.label: Land use
classes.comment:
Land use of the product.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: LCA result
classes.comment: A measurable outcome of a life cycle assessment, representing the quantified effect of a product.

classes.label: Length
classes.comment: Length of the product

classes.label: Location
classes.comment: A generic location representing a spatial entity that can serve as a context in an event. A location may play different roles depending on the event context, such as observation point or business location.
classes.source: Defined for the EU DPP Core Ontology Event module to support generic location references in event contexts.

classes.label: Maintenance
classes.comment: Actions (one or more) taken to keep a product in a condition where it can fulfil its intended purpose. ESPR Art 2(19).

classes.label: Making Available on the Market
classes.comment: Any supply of a product for distribution, consumption or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge. ESPR Art 2(39).

classes.label: Material footprint
classes.comment:
Material footprint
refers to the total amount of raw materials extracted to meet final consumption demands. (ESPR Art 2 (26))

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Material of composition
classes.comment: Material the product (or component) is made of [ESPR Annex I]. Material as an element of composition.

classes.label: Material type
classes.comment:
Placeholder class for material type classification applicable in a sector or mandated by a delegated act (DA).

Potential types could be, on the example of textile sector: cotton, nylon, ...

classes.label: Method
classes.comment: LCIA methods allow to transform and aggregate emissions to the environment and resource use data into a limited set of interpretable and reportable impact potential scores. (Adapted from LCAnet Ontology, SmartACV Project, Version 1.0, 2025)

classes.label: Methodology
classes.comment:
Related LCIA methods can be grouped under LCIA methodologies. (ILCD Handbook, General guidance). 
Examples of methodologies include EN15804+A2, EF v3.1, Impact World.

classes.label: Microplastic release
classes.comment:
Product parameters as listed in the ESPR Annex I :

(p) microplastic and nano plastic release as expressed through the release during relevant
product life cycle stages, including manufacturing, transport, use and end of life stages;

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Nanoplastic release
classes.comment:
Product parameters as listed in the ESPR Annex I :

(p) microplastic and nano plastic release as expressed through the release during relevant
product life cycle stages, including manufacturing, transport, use and end of life stages;

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Natural Person
classes.comment: A human being as distinguished from a person (as a corporation) created by operation of law

classes.label: Object Event
classes.comment: A technical event carrier representing an action performed on one or more identifiable objects, captured either at instance level or at class-and-quantity level. Each ObjectEvent has exactly one action type and includes at least one instance-level identifier, at least one quantity context, or both.
classes.source: GS1 EPCIS 2.0; adapted from the Event module mapping table.

classes.label: Other Technical Specification
classes.comment: Other technical specifications in relation to which conformity is declared.

classes.label: Ozone Depletion Footprint
classes.comment: Quantifies the potential stratospheric ozone layer depletion caused by substances emitted by a product throughout its life cycle. It is an ImpactResult linked to the Ozone Depletion impact category.

classes.label: Packaging waste amount
classes.comment:
Packaging waste amount of the product.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Placing on the Market
classes.comment: The very first time a product is made available on the Union market. ESPR Art 2(40).

classes.label: Plastic release
classes.comment:
Product parameters as listed in the ESPR Annex I :

(p) microplastic and nano plastic release as expressed through the release during relevant
product life cycle stages, including manufacturing, transport, use and end of life stages;

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Plastics waste amount
classes.comment:
Hazardous waste amount of the product.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Product
classes.comment: Product means any physical goods that are placed on the market or put into service. ESPR Art 2 (1))

classes.label: Product dimension
classes.comment:
Dimension class covers measurements of length, width, height, volume, and weight of the product required by
ESPR Annex I in its product parameters

classes.label: Product Event
classes.comment: An ESPR-level event concept representing an event that affects the state, condition, use, circulation, transformation, maintenance, or end-of-life status of a product. A ProductEvent captures the product-facing semantics of the occurrence and is distinct from any DPP-side event that may be triggered to record or reflect it.

classes.label: Product Requirement
classes.comment: Product requirements means a requirement to be fullfilled by a product when placed on the market.

classes.label: Product to packaging ratio
classes.comment:
ESPR Annex I, the list of product parameters includes the parameter called the  product to packaging ratio.

However, it is not specified in ESPR  whether that ratio is defined on the basis of weight or on the basis of volume.

**This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.**

classes.label: Property
classes.comment: A property of the product.

classes.label: Putting into Service
classes.comment: The first use of a product for its intended purpose in the Union. ESPR Art 2(41).

classes.label: Quality indicator
classes.comment:
Product characteristics like durability and reliability.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Quantitative Property
classes.comment: A property (respectively measurand of a property) of the product (model) that is expressed by a quantity value. A specific quantity.

classes.label: Quantity Element
classes.comment: A structure representing a class-level identification context together with quantity information. It is used when an event refers to objects at class level rather than to individually identified instances.
classes.source: Adapted from GS1 EPCIS quantity list semantics for the EU DPP Core Ontology Event module.

classes.label: Read Point
classes.comment: A location playing the role of observation point, indicating where the event was physically captured or observed.
classes.source: GS1 EPCIS 2.0; read point concept adapted for the Event module.

classes.label: Recoverable rate
classes.comment: This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Recycled materials use
classes.comment:
Recycled materials use of the product.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Recycling collection rate
classes.comment: This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Recycling rate
classes.comment: This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Refurbishment
classes.comment: Actions carried out to prepare, clean, test, service and, where necessary, repair a product or a discarded product in order to restore its performance or functionality within the intended use and range of performance originally conceived at the design stage at the time of the placing of the product on the market. ESPR Art 2(18).

classes.label: Reliability
classes.comment:
Reliability
means the probability that a product functions as required under given conditions for a given
duration without an occurrence which results in a primary or secondary function of the product no
longer being performed. (ESPR Art 2 (16))

Reliability is usually expressed in terms of mean time between failures (MTBF), which is the average length of time that a device will operate without failure.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Remanufacturing
classes.comment: Actions through which a new product is produced from objects that are waste, products or components and through which at least one change is made that substantially affects the safety, performance, purpose or type of the product. ESPR Art 2(16).

classes.label: Repair
classes.comment: Actions taken to return a defective product or waste to a condition where it fulfils its intended purpose. ESPR Art 2(20).

classes.label: Resource consumption
classes.comment:
Resource consumption of the product.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Source or Destination
classes.comment: A contextual structure representing a source or a destination associated with an event in relation to a business transfer.
classes.source: GS1 EPCIS 2.0; source and destination list structure adapted for the Event module.

classes.label: Source or Destination Entity
classes.comment: An intermediate alignment class used to represent an entity that can play the role of source or destination in an event context. Its precise alignment to Actor, Organisation, Location, or other external concepts is intended to be specified in the mapping ontology.
classes.source: Defined for the EU DPP Core Ontology Event module as an intermediate alignment point.

classes.label: Source or Destination Type
classes.comment: A classification indicating the business meaning of a source or destination associated with an event.
classes.source: GS1 EPCIS and CBV source/destination type semantics adapted for the Event module.

classes.label: Substance
classes.comment: Means a chemical element and its compounds in the natural state or obtained by any manufacturing process, including any additive necessary to preserve its stability and any impurity deriving from the process used, but excluding any solvent which may be separated without affecting the stability of the substance or changing its composition; ESPR Art 2, Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006

classes.label: Substance of concern
classes.comment: means a substance that:(a) meets the criteria laid down in Article 57 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 and is identified in accordance with Article 59(1) of that Regulation; (b) is classified in Part 3 of Annex VI to Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 in one of the following hazard classes or hazard categories: (i) carcinogenicity categories 1 and 2; (ii) germ cell mutagenicity categories 1 and 2; (iii) reproductive toxicity categories 1 and 2; (iv) endocrine disruption for human health categories 1 and 2; (v) endocrine disruption for the environment categories 1 and 2; (vi) persistent, mobile and toxic or very persistent, very mobile properties; (vii) persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic or very persistent, very bioaccumulative properties; (viii) respiratory sensitisation category 1; (ix) skin sensitisation category 1; (x) hazardous to the aquatic environment — categories chronic 1 to 4; (xi) hazardous to the ozone layer; (xii) specific target organ toxicity — repeated exposure categories 1 and 2; (xiii) specific target organ toxicity — single exposure categories 1 and 2; (c) is regulated under Regulation (EU) 2019/1021; or (d) negatively affects the reuse and recycling of materials in the product in which it is present [ESPR Art 2(10)]

classes.label: Sustainable renewable materials use
classes.comment:
Sustainable renewable materials use of the product.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Technical Specification
classes.comment: Technical specification means a document that prescribes technical requirements to be fulfilled by a product, process, service or system and which lays down one or more of the following: Common Specification or Other Technical Specification.

classes.label: Threshold of substance of concern
classes.comment:
Relevant threshold of Substance of Concern.

By default, information on all substances of concern present in a product, above the  relevant thresholds, should be included in the DPP [ESPR FAQ 10.115, p59]

classes.label: Threshold of substance of concern
classes.comment:
Relevant threshold of Substance of Concern.

By default, information on all substances of concern present in a product, above the  relevant thresholds, should be included in the DPP [ESPR FAQ 10.115, p59]

classes.label: Toxicity Footprint
classes.comment: Quantifies the potential human health and ecological toxicity impacts of a product over its life cycle. ToxicityFootprint aggregates relevant ImpactCategories such as Human Toxicity (cancer and non-cancer) and Ecotoxicity.

classes.label: Transaction Event
classes.comment: A technical event carrier representing the association or disassociation of one or more identifiable objects with one or more business transactions. Each TransactionEvent has exactly one action type, is linked to at least one business transaction context, and includes at least one instance-level identifier, at least one quantity context, or both. It provides documentary or contextual linkage and shall not by itself be interpreted as a lifecycle transition.
classes.source: GS1 EPCIS 2.0; adapted from the Event module mapping table.

classes.label: Transformation
classes.comment: An identified transformation resource used to correlate one or more TransformationEvents that describe the same transformation.
classes.source: Adapted from GS1 EPCIS and CBV transformation identifier semantics for the Event module.

classes.label: Transformation Event
classes.comment: A technical event carrier representing the transformation of one or more input objects into one or more output objects, capturing material or structural change across event inputs and outputs. Each TransformationEvent includes at least one input context and at least one output context, expressed at instance level, quantity level, or both. It may refer to an identified transformation used to correlate multiple events describing the same transformation.
classes.source: GS1 EPCIS 2.0; adapted from the Event module mapping table.

classes.label: Union Harmonised Legislation
classes.comment: Union Harmonisation Legislation shall mean any Union legislation harmonising the conditions for the marketing of products. Examples are directives, regulations and delegated acts.
classes.source:
Decision No 768/2008/EC Annex I Art R1 (17)
https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dec/2008/768(1)/oj#anx_I

classes.label: Upgrading
classes.comment: Actions carried out to enhance the functionality, performance, capacity, safety or aesthetics of a product. ESPR Art 2(17).

classes.label: Volume
classes.comment: Volume of the product

classes.label: Waste generation amount
classes.comment:
Waste generation amount of the product.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Water consumption
classes.comment:
Water consumption of the product.

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

classes.label: Weight
classes.comment: Weight of the product

classes.label: Width
classes.comment: Width of the product

properties.label: Abbreviation
properties.comment: The abbreviation used for the Substance of Concern; [ESPR Article 7(5)]

properties.label: according to
properties.comment: Property defining specifies conformity assess procedure/cerfication scheme underlying the cerfificate.

properties.label: Actor name
properties.comment: Name of an actor.

properties.label: allows Conformity Assessment Module
properties.comment: A property that specifies the conformity assment procedure applicable to the type of product

properties.label: Applies to product
properties.comment: The property links DPP and the Product.

properties.label: assigned ELI
properties.comment: Standardised identification that makes it easier to identify and describe legislation across Europe.

properties.label: Assignment valid from
properties.comment: The date and time from which the actor role assignment is valid.

properties.label: Assignment valid to
properties.comment: The date and time until which the actor role assignment is valid.

properties.label: has business transaction identifier
properties.comment: Specifies the identifier of a business transaction associated with an event.
properties.source: Adapted from GS1 EPCIS business transaction identifier semantics for the Event module.

properties.label: certificateNumber
properties.comment: Number of the certificate

properties.label: certificate revision number
properties.comment: Number of the revision of a certificate

properties.label: class identifier
properties.comment: The class-level identifier used in a quantity element, such as a GTIN, LGTIN, or another EPC class identifier.
properties.source: Adapted from EPCIS class-level identification semantics.

properties.label: Classification code set
properties.comment:
The product classification code set.

See also Produc hasProductGroup ClassificationCode documentation.

properties.label: Classification code value
properties.comment: Classification code value from the Classification code set.

properties.label: Commodity code
properties.comment: Relevant commodity codes, such as a TARIC code as defined in Council Regulation (EEC) No 2658/87.[ESPR Annex III (d)]

properties.label: Concerns DPP
properties.comment:
Links a DPP event to the Digital Product Passport whose content, state, or accessibility is affected by the event. This property captures information-level changes and is not intended to represent physical or operational events on the product.

DPP is modelled in the EU DPP CO P_DPP module.
DPPEvent is modelled in the EU DPP CO EVENT module.

properties.label: Concerns product
properties.comment:
Links a product event to the product whose state, condition, or lifecycle is affected by the event.

Product is modelled in the EU DPP CO P_DPP module.
ProductEvent is modelled in the EU DPP CO EVENT module.

properties.label: Conformity attested by
properties.comment:
Specifies the notified body that attest the product's conformity with Union harmonisation legislation. 

UnionHarmonisationLegislation is modelled in the EU DPP CO COMP module.
Actor is modelled in the EU DPP CO ACTOR module.

properties.label: conformity declared to
properties.comment: A property which specifies which Union Harmonisation Legislation conformity is declared to.

properties.label: Contains substance of concern
properties.comment:
Linking the product to a substance of concern the product contains.

Product is modelled in the EU DPP CO P_DPP module.
Substance of concern is modelled in the EU DPP CO SOC module.

properties.label: Content type
properties.comment: Content type of a document. Can be only “application” or “pdf”.

properties.label: Description
properties.comment: Product description

properties.label: Dictionary reference
properties.comment:
The reference to the unique identifier of the data point specification defined in the repository/data dictionary.

It is formatted as a URI/URL .

properties.label: dpp event recorded at
properties.comment: The date and time at which the technical record of a DPP event was created in an information system or audit trail.

properties.label: dpp event record identifier
properties.comment: A unique identifier assigned to a DPP event record.

properties.label: DPP status
properties.comment: The status of the DPP instance as digital resource.

properties.label: event identifier
properties.comment: A unique identifier assigned to the event.
properties.source: GS1 EPCIS 1.2 and 2.0; optional event identifier adapted for the Event module.

properties.label: event time
properties.comment: The date and time at which the event occurred.
properties.source: GS1 EPCIS 2.0; core event time property used in the Event module.

properties.label: event time zone offset
properties.comment: The time zone offset in effect at the time and place where the event occurred.
properties.source: GS1 EPCIS 2.0; core event time zone offset property used in the Event module.

enumerations.label: Action Type
enumerations.comment: Specifies the business action associated with an event carrier, indicating how the event relates to the lifecycle of the involved objects.

values.label: ADD
values.comment: Indicates that objects are being added to the context of the event, such as being commissioned or aggregated.

values.label: DELETE
values.comment: Indicates that objects are removed from the context of the event, such as being decommissioned or disaggregated.

values.label: OBSERVE
values.comment: Indicates that objects are observed in the event context without changing their lifecycle state.

values.label: GLN
values.comment:
A globally unique identifier defined by GS1 used to identify legal entities, functional entities, and physical locations within business and supply chain processes.

Typically identifies: legal entities, functional entities (departments), physical locations (warehouses, sites).

values.label: LEI
values.comment:
A Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) is a globally unique 20-character alphanumeric code that identifies legally distinct entities participating in financial transactions, as defined by ISO 17442.

A 20‑character code used globally for financial and regulatory reporting.
Required for companies involved in financial transactions.
Used by regulators, banks, customs, and some trade systems.

enumerations.label: Authority role
enumerations.comment: Parent class for roles of authorities, such as market surveillance authority, customs authority, etc.

values.label: Customs Authority
values.comment: Customs authorities means  customs authorities as defined in point 1 of Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013; [Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, Art 3 (24)]

values.label: Market Surveillance Authority
values.comment: Market surveillance authority means an authority designated by a Member State under Article 10 as responsible for carrying out market surveillance in the territory of that Member State; [Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 Art 3 (4)]

enumerations.label: Business Step
enumerations.comment: A classification indicating the immediate business context of an EPCIS-inspired event.

values.label: commissioning
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to the creation or initial introduction of objects into the system.

values.label: destroying
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to the destruction of objects.

values.label: inspecting
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to inspecting objects for quality or compliance.

values.label: loading
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to loading objects onto a transport or container.

values.label: other
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to a business step not explicitly covered by the predefined categories.

values.label: packing
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to packing objects into a container or packaging hierarchy.

values.label: receiving
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to receiving objects at a location.

values.label: repackaging
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to repackaging objects into new packaging configurations.

values.label: repairing
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to repairing objects to restore their functionality.

values.label: retail selling
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to selling objects to end consumers.

values.label: shipping
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to shipping objects from one location to another.

values.label: stocking
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to placing objects into stock or inventory.

values.label: storing
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to storing objects at a location.

values.label: transporting
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to transporting objects between locations.

values.label: unloading
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to unloading objects from a transport or container.

values.label: unpacking
values.comment: Indicates that the event corresponds to removing objects from a container or packaging hierarchy.

enumerations.label: Carbon footprint
enumerations.comment:
Carbon footprint
means the sum of greenhouse gas emissions and greenhouse gas removals in a product system, expressed as CO equivalents and based on a life cycle assessment using the single impact category
of climate change. (ESPR Art 2 25))

This class description needs to be extended/specialised according to the corresponding delegated acts or/and industry standards.

enumerations.label: Characterization Factor
enumerations.comment: Also called Impact factors, are factors that quantify the relative impact of different substances within the same category. These factors are used to convert the number of emissions into impact scores for each category. (LCAnet Ontology, SmartACV Project, Version 1.0, 2025)

values.label: Global warming potential (GWP) over a 100-year time horizon

enumerations.label: Characterization Model
enumerations.comment:
A characterization model provides a mathematical framework, as a set of equations, to quantify an impact category based on the chosen method. A characterization model is used by a method. (LCAnet Ontology, SmartACV Project, Version 1.0, 2025) 
Example: IPCC (2021) AR6.

enumerations.label: Circular economy role
enumerations.comment: Parent class for roles related to circular economy, such as remanufacturer, refurbisher, etc.

values.label: Independent Operator
values.comment: Independent operator means natural or legal person that is independent of the manufacturer and is directly or indirectly involved in the refurbishment, repair, maintenance or repurposing of a product, and includes waste management operators, refurbishers, repairers, manufacturers or distributors of repair equipment, tools or spare parts, as well as publishers of technical information, operators offering inspection and testing services and operators offering training for installers, manufacturers and repairers of equipment; [ESPR Art 2 (47)]

values.label: Professional Repairer
values.comment: Professional repairer means a natural or legal person that provides professional repair or maintenance services for a product, irrespective of whether that person acts within the manufacturer’s distribution system or independently; [ESPR Art 2 (48)]

values.label: Recycler
values.comment: An actor performing recycling, which means "any recovery operation by which waste materials are reprocessed into products, materials or substances whether for the original or other purposes. It includes the reprocessing of organic material but does not include energy recovery and the reprocessing into materials that are to be used as fuels or for backfilling operations" [WFD Art 3 (17)]

values.label: Refurbisher
values.comment: An actor performing refurbishment, which means "actions carried out to prepare, clean, test, service and, where necessary, repair a product or a discarded product in order to restore its performance or functionality within the intended use and range of performance originally conceived at the design stage at the time of the placing of the product on the market."; [ESPR Art 2 (18)]

values.label: Remanufacturer
values.comment: An actor performing remanufacturing, which means "actions through which a new product is produced from objects that are waste, products or components and through which at least one change is made that substantially affects the safety, performance, purpose or type of the product"; [ESPR Art 2 (16)]

enumerations.label: Conformity assessment role
enumerations.comment: Conformity assessment means the process demonstrating whether the ecodesign requirements set out in the relevant delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4 have been fulfilled; [ESPR Art 2 (51)]

values.label: Conformity Assessment Body
values.comment: Conformity assessment body means a body that performs conformity assessment activities including calibration, testing, certification and inspection; [ESPR Art 2 (52)]

values.label: Notified Body
values.comment: Notified body means a conformity assessment body notified in accordance with Chapter IX.; [ESPR Art 2 (53)]

enumerations.label: Disposition
enumerations.comment: A classification indicating the business state of the object or objects following an EPCIS-inspired event.

values.label: active
values.comment: Indicates that the object is active and in normal use following the event.

values.label: available
values.comment: Indicates that the object is available for use, sale, or processing following the event.

values.label: damaged
values.comment: Indicates that the object is damaged following the event.

values.label: destroyed
values.comment: Indicates that the object has been destroyed and is no longer usable.

values.label: disposed
values.comment: Indicates that the object has been disposed of following the event.

values.label: expired
values.comment: Indicates that the object has reached its expiration date.

values.label: in transit
values.comment: Indicates that the object is in transit between locations following the event.

values.label: recalled
values.comment: Indicates that the object has been recalled from the market or supply chain.

values.label: reserved
values.comment: Indicates that the object is reserved and not available for general use or sale.

values.label: returned
values.comment: Indicates that the object has been returned following the event.

values.label: sellable accessible
values.comment: Indicates that the object is sellable and physically accessible.

values.label: sellable not accessible
values.comment: Indicates that the object is sellable but not physically accessible.

values.label: stolen
values.comment: Indicates that the object has been stolen.

values.label: unknown
values.comment: Indicates that the state of the object is unknown following the event.

enumerations.label: DPP Action Type
enumerations.comment: A classification indicating the type of information-level action performed during a DPP update event.

values.label: add data
values.comment: Indicates that new information is added to the Digital Product Passport.

values.label: correct data
values.comment: Indicates that erroneous, inconsistent, or incomplete information in the Digital Product Passport is corrected.

values.label: delete data
values.comment: Indicates that information is removed from the Digital Product Passport.

values.label: modify data
values.comment: Indicates that existing information in the Digital Product Passport is modified.

enumerations.label: Economic operator role
enumerations.comment: Economic operator means the manufacturer, the authorised representative, the importer, the distributor, the dealer and the fulfilment service provider; [ESPR Art 2 (46)]

values.label: Authorised Representative
values.comment: Authorised representative means any natural or legal person established in the Union that has received a written mandate from the manufacturer to act on the manufacturer’s behalf in relation to specified tasks with regard to the manufacturer’s obligations under this Regulation; [ESPR Art 2 (43)]

values.label: Dealer
values.comment: Dealer means a distributor or any other natural or legal person that offers products for sale, hire or hire purchase, or that displays products, to end users in the course of a commercial activity, including through distance selling; and includes any natural or legal person that puts a product into service in the course of a commercial activity; [ESPR Art 2 (55)]

values.label: Distributor
values.comment: Distributor means any natural or legal person in the supply chain, other than the manufacturer or the importer, that makes a product available on the market; [ESPR Art 2 (45)]

values.label: Fulfilment Service Provider
values.comment: Fulfilment service provider means any natural or legal person offering, in the course of commercial activity, at least two of the following services: warehousing, packaging, addressing and dispatching, without having ownership of the products involved, excluding postal services as defined in point 1 of Article 2 of Directive 97/67/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council (31), parcel delivery services as defined in point 2 of Article 2 of Regulation (EU) 2018/644 of the European Parliament and of the Council (32), and any other postal services or freight transport services; [Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 Art 3 (11)].

values.label: Importer
values.comment: Importer means any natural or legal person established in the Union that places a product from a third country on the Union market; [ESPR Art 2 (44)]

values.label: Manufacturer
values.comment: Manufacturer means any natural or legal person that manufactures a product or that has a product designed or manufactured and markets that product under their name or trademark; [ESPR Art 2 (42)]

enumerations.label: Emission Flow
enumerations.comment: A type of flow representing substances released to the environment during a product’s life cycle.

enumerations.label: End user role
enumerations.comment: Parent class for roles of end users, such as consumer, etc.

values.label: Consumer
values.comment: Consumer means any natural person who, in relation to contracts covered by Directive (EU) 2019/771, is acting for purposes which are outside that person's trade, business, craft or profession; [Directive (EU) 2019/771, Art 2 (2)]

values.label: Customer
values.comment: Customer means a natural or legal person that purchases, hires or receives a product for their own use whether or not acting for purposes which are outside their trade, business, craft or profession; [ESPR Art 2 (35)]

values.label: End User
values.comment: End user means any natural or legal person residing or established in the Union, to whom a product has been made available either as a consumer outside of any trade, business, craft or profession or as a professional end user in the course of its industrial or professional activities; [Regulation (EU) 2019/1020  Art 3 (21)]

enumerations.label: Flow result
enumerations.comment: A type of LCAResult that quantifies the flows of materials, energy, or emissions associated with a product

values.label: Resource use, minerals and metals
values.comment: Measures the amount of mineral and metal resources consumed by a product system. Represented as FlowResult of type MineralsAndMetalsFlow. Can be used to calculate the MaterialFootprint.

enumerations.label: Fossil Energy Footprint
enumerations.comment: Quantifies the consumption of fossil energy (coal, oil, natural gas) by a product during its life cycle. It is a specialized EnergyFootprint and a FlowResult with FlowType FossilEnergy.

values.label: Resource use, fossils
values.comment: Measures the amount of fossil resources consumed by a product system, including coal, oil, and natural gas. Represented as FlowResult of type FossilResourceFlow.

enumerations.label: Impact Category
enumerations.comment: An impact category represents a specific environmental issue that the LCA aims to assess, such as global warming or ozone depletion. Each category aggregates the effects of different emissions that contribute to the same environmental problem. (LCAnet Ontology, SmartACV Project, Version 1.0, 2025) An impact category is classified as whether is corresponds to environmental impact, social impact, etc.

values.label: Acidification
values.comment: Measures the potential of a product system's emissions to cause acidification in ecosystems (soil, water, vegetation), mainly from SO₂, NOx, and NH₃ emissions.

values.label: Eutrophication, freshwater
values.comment: Measures potential nutrient enrichment of freshwater ecosystems due to emissions of N and P compounds, causing effects such as algal blooms.

values.label: Eutrophication, marine
values.comment: Measures potential nutrient enrichment of marine ecosystems due to emissions of N and P compounds.

values.label: Eutrophication, Terrestial
values.comment: Measures potential nutrient enrichment of terrestrial ecosystems due to nitrogen deposition.

values.label: Human toxicity, cancer
values.comment: Measures the potential carcinogenic effects of a product system on humans due to chemical emissions.

values.label: Human toxicity, non-cancer
values.comment: Measures the potential non-carcinogenic effects of a product system on humans due to chemical emissions.

values.label: Ionising radiation, human health
values.comment: Measures the potential human health impact of ionizing radiation due to a product system, including exposure to radioactive substances.

values.label: Land use (occupation and transformation)
values.comment: Measures the potential environmental impact of land occupation and transformation due to a product system, including both the area of land used and its conversion from one type to another.

values.label: Ozone depletion
values.comment: Measures the potential reduction of the stratospheric ozone layer caused by emissions of ozone-depleting substances in a product system.

values.label: Particulate matter
values.comment: Measures the potential human health impacts of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) emitted by a product system, including respiratory and cardiovascular effects.

values.label: Photochemical ozone formation, human health
values.comment: Measures the potential human health impact of photochemical ozone formation (smog) due to VOCs and NOx emissions from a product system.

enumerations.label: Impact Category Indicator
enumerations.comment:
An impact category refers to a specific metric/measurable quantity that is used to quantify an impact category. (LCAnet Ontology, SmartACV Project, Version 1.0, 2025)
Examples include: Global Warming Potential (GWP) and Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP).

values.label: Fraction of nutrients reaching freshwater end compartment (P)
Fraction of nutrients reaching marine end compartment (N)
Human exposure efficiency relative to U235

enumerations.label: Impact Type
enumerations.comment: A category representing the type of an impact category measured in a life cycle assessment. Each ImpactType classifies ImpactCategories according to the area of concern, such as environmental, social, economic, or human health.

enumerations.label: Legal Person
enumerations.comment: A body of persons or an entity (as a corporation) considered as having many of the rights and responsibilities of a natural person and especially the capacity to sue and be sued.

values.label: European Commission
values.comment: The European Commission, abbreviated as EC, is the executive branch of the European Union.

enumerations.label: Life Cycle Stage
enumerations.comment: A phase in the life cycle of a product, from raw material acquisition through production, use, and end-of-life, in accordance with life cycle concepts defined in ISO 14040 and ISO 14044

values.label: Distribution
values.comment: Stage involving transport and distribution of the product to the market.

values.label: End Of Life
values.comment: Stage involving disposal, recycling, or recovery of the product.

values.label: Manufacturing
values.comment: Stage involving material processing and product manufacturing.

values.label: Raw Material Acquisition
values.comment: Stage involving extraction and acquisition of raw materials.

values.label: Use
values.comment: Stage during which the product is used by the end user.

values.label: CAS
values.comment: CAS Number (Chemical Abstracts Service)

enumerations.label: Origin of material
enumerations.comment: Origin of the material used in product [ESPR Annex I]

values.label: raw
values.comment: Raw material

values.label: recycled
values.comment: Recycled material

values.label: renewable
values.comment: Renewable material

values.label: batch
values.comment: According to ESPR Art 9 (2d) the digital product passport is to be established at model, batch or item level, and the definition of such levels is given by delegated acts;

values.label: item
values.comment: According to ESPR Art 9 (2d) the digital product passport is to be established at model, batch or item level, and the definition of such levels is given by delegated acts;

values.label: model
values.comment: According to ESPR Art 9 (2d) the digital product passport is to be established at model, batch or item level, and the definition of such levels is given by delegated acts;

values.label: GTIN
values.comment: A globally unique identifier for trade items, defined by GS1, used to identify products at various packaging levels.

values.label: SKU
values.comment: A Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) is an internal identifier assigned by an organization to uniquely identify and track a product, item, or variant within its own inventory and management systems.

enumerations.label: Resource Flow
enumerations.comment: A type of flow representing the consumption or use of natural resources throughout a product’s life cycle.

enumerations.label: Role
enumerations.comment: Role means a set of tasks typically performed by one actor. (e.g. Responsible Economic Operator, Independent operator); [CIRPASS-2 User Stories 3.1]

values.label: Credential Agency
values.comment: A legal person that provides (professional) credentials to parties, which may be used to make and verify a variety of claims in the DPP, (ESPR) Art. 11 last paragraph. For example, a credentials agency could certify a professional repairer and provide appropriate credentials for the DPP system; [CIRPASS-2 User Stories 3.1]

values.label: DPP Service Provider
values.comment: Digital product passport service provider means a natural or legal person that is an independent third-party authorised by the economic operator which places the product on the market or puts it into service and that processes the digital product passport data for that product for the purpose of making such data available to economic operators and other relevant actors with a right to access those data under this Regulation or other Union law; [ESPR Art 2 (32)]

values.label: Issuing Agency
values.comment: Issuing agency is a legal persons that provide unique identifiers and data carriers Art 12 (4a). Under specific conditions, economic operators may perform the functions associated with an Issuing Agency; [ESPR Art 12 (4b)]

enumerations.label: Water Footrpint
enumerations.comment: Quantifies the freshwater consumption associated with a product throughout its life cycle. WaterFootprint is a FlowResult linked to the Water FlowType.
